default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-998.title: Seasonal minute-of-day drift follow
E-998.hypothesis: The forward return from a given minute of the day has a persistent sign (scheduled flows, fixings, participant rhythm); when the last 20 sessions agree strongly, take that side.

E-999.title: Autocorrelation regime switch
E-999.hypothesis: When recent bar returns are negatively autocorrelated the market is in a bounce regime (fade the big bar); when positively autocorrelated it is in a push regime (follow the big bar).

E-1000.title: VWAP standard-deviation band fade
E-1000.hypothesis: Price stretching beyond k standard deviations of its own session distance to VWAP is an outlier for that day's volatility; liquidity providers anchored to VWAP lean against it.

E-1001.title: Intraday-profile deviation fade
E-1001.hypothesis: Compared with the average path of the last 20 sessions at the same minute, a day that has run much further than the usual profile has pulled forward the move; fade the excess.

E-1002.title: Regression-slope t-stat trend follow
E-1002.hypothesis: A statistically significant linear slope of recent closes (t-stat) separates a real directional flow from noise; follow when the t-stat first crosses the threshold.

E-1003.title: Index-dollar inverse confirmation follow
E-1003.hypothesis: WIN rising while the dollar falls (or vice versa), both by more than usual, is the macro risk-on/off link agreeing with itself; foreign flow keeps pushing the index the same way.

E-1004.title: Three-EMA ribbon alignment follow
E-1004.hypothesis: When price and three EMAs of increasing length line up in order, short, medium and slow holders are all on the same side; the first aligned bar starts a trend leg.

E-1005.title: Low-overlap trend-bar follow
E-1005.hypothesis: Consecutive bars that barely overlap the previous bar's range mean one side is absorbing all liquidity without negotiation; follow the net move.

E-1006.title: Stalled-close release follow
E-1006.hypothesis: A stretch where many bars close at exactly the same price means resting orders are pinning the tape; the first bar that closes away from the pin shows which side gave in.

E-1007.title: Busy-day EMA and VWAP agreement follow
E-1007.hypothesis: On sessions where cumulative volume runs well above the same-time norm, trends persist; price regaining both its EMA and VWAP on the same side is a pullback ending.
